chapters.title: Chapter 4: Tax and Rules in India

lessons.title: The Startup ESOP Tax Deferral: Who Qualifies and How It Works

children.text: The cruellest feature of Indian ESOPs is the one you already met in Chapter 2: you owe tax the moment you exercise, even when the shares cannot be sold. Parliament noticed. The fix, introduced in 2020 and carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025, lets employees of a narrow category of startups postpone that payment.
Narrow is the operative word. Most employees who assume they qualify do not.

body.text: The deferral does not reduce your tax. It moves the payment date. And it applies only if your employer holds a specific certificate that roughly one in fifty recognised startups actually has.

children.text: Two Gates, Not One
To offer the deferral, your employer must be an eligible startup under Section 140 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 [Section 80-IAC of the Income-tax Act, 1961]. That means clearing two separate gates:
DPIIT recognition
, which many startups have, and an
Inter-Ministerial Board certificate
, which very few do.

markDefs.definition: Recognition granted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade to entities meeting the official definition of a startup.
The Inter-Ministerial Board, whose certificate an already DPIIT-recognised startup needs to claim the tax holiday and to offer its employees the ESOP tax deferral.

body.label: Startups holding the certification needed to offer the deferral
body.context: Roughly 4,000 startups, against well over a lakh with DPIIT recognition. Reported figures, and the gap is the whole point.

body.title: DPIIT recognition and IMB certification are not the same thing

children.text: DPIIT recognition is the broad, relatively accessible status: an eligible entity under ten years old, below the turnover threshold, working on innovation or a scalable business model. Thousands of companies hold it, and it brings various benefits.

The Inter-Ministerial Board certificate is a further, much harder approval, and it is what unlocks the income tax holiday under Section 140 and, in turn, the ESOP deferral for employees. A company can be DPIIT recognised, well funded and genuinely innovative, and still not have it.
So the practical question to your employer is not "are we a DPIIT startup". It is "do we hold an Inter-Ministerial Board certificate, and can our employees defer ESOP perquisite tax".

body.text: Do not plan an exercise around the deferral until you have seen written confirmation from your employer that it qualifies. Assuming eligibility and discovering otherwise leaves you with a tax bill due immediately, on shares you cannot sell.

children.text: What the Deferral Actually Does
The
perquisite
is still computed the same way at exercise: fair market value on the exercise date minus what you paid. What changes is when the
TDS
and the tax must be paid. Under Section 392(3) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 [Section 192(1C) of the 1961 Act], payment shifts to the earliest of three events.

markDefs.definition: A benefit received from employment that is taxed as salary, such as the discount on shares received through an ESOP.
Tax Deducted at Source: tax the employer withholds and deposits on your behalf.

body.caption: The three triggers, whichever comes first

cells: Reported as 60 months from the end of the tax year of allotment for shares allotted on or after 1 April 2026, and 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year under the earlier regime
Sell even a part and the tax on that allotment becomes payable
Resignation or termination ends the deferral, regardless of how much time was left

body.text: Read the third trigger again. The deferral is tied to staying. An employee who exercises under the deferral and then changes jobs a year later pays the tax at that point, with no sale and no cash. The benefit rewards people who stay until a liquidity event, which is exactly what it was designed to do.

children.text: One Employee, Two Worlds
Ananya exercises 4,000 options at an exercise price of ₹10 when the fair market value is ₹260. Her perquisite is ₹10,00,000, and at a 30% slab with cess the tax is ₹3,12,000.

body.title: The same exercise, with and without the deferral

columns.label: No deferral
points: Pays ₹3,12,000 of tax immediately, via TDS from salary
Total outflow of ₹3,52,000 in the same year
Holds illiquid shares and has funded the tax from savings

columns.label: With the deferral
points: Payment falls due on sale, on leaving, or at the end of the window
Cash stays with her until one of those events arrives

body.title: How the clock runs for an allotment in August 2026

events.title: Exercise and allotment
events.description: Perquisite of ₹10,00,000 is computed and reported, but the tax is not collected yet.

events.title: End of the tax year of allotment
events.description: The deferral window is measured from this date, not from the exercise date.

events.title: A sale or an exit ends it early
events.description: Selling the shares or leaving the company makes the deferred tax payable within the statutory timeline.

events.title: Window expires
events.description: On the 60-month reading for allotments from 1 April 2026, the tax falls due even if the shares are still unsold and still illiquid.

body.title: Size the Deferred Amount
body.prompt: Ananya exercises 4,000 options at ₹10 when the FMV is ₹260. At an effective rate of 31.2%, how much perquisite tax is being deferred?
body.explanation: Perquisite = (₹260 minus ₹10) × 4,000 = ₹10,00,000. At 31.2%, that is ₹3,12,000. She still pays ₹40,000 to exercise today; only the tax waits.

body.title: Which Trigger Fires First?
body.question: Rahul works at an eligible startup and exercises in June 2027 under the deferral. In March 2029 he sells a quarter of his shares in a company buyback. In September 2030 he resigns. When does the deferred tax on that allotment become payable?
options: In March 2029, when he sells part of the shares
Only when the deferral window expires
Proportionately, a quarter in 2029 and the rest on resignation
body.explanation: The rule is the earliest of the three triggers, and a sale is one of them. The first event in time was the March 2029 sale, so that is when the deferred perquisite tax on the allotment falls due, not merely on the portion sold.

body.title: Confirming You Actually Qualify
steps: Ask whether the company holds an Inter-Ministerial Board certificate, not just DPIIT recognition.
Ask for that confirmation in writing from finance or HR, not verbally.
Check whether the deferral is being applied to your allotment specifically.
Note the date of allotment, since the window is measured from the end of that tax year.
Ask how the deferred perquisite will appear in your Form 16 and your return.
Ask what happens operationally if you resign, since the company must still collect the tax.
Plan the cash for the tax anyway, because every trigger arrives eventually.

children.text: The Honest Limits of This Relief
It is a postponement, not a discount.
The liability is computed at exercise and does not shrink if the shares later fall in value.
Leaving ends it.
The trigger that catches most people is resignation, which is common well within five years.
The window can expire before liquidity does.
A startup with no buyback and no listing by year five leaves you paying tax on shares you still cannot sell.
Coverage is tiny.
Reported figures suggest only around 2% of recognised startups hold the certification needed, so most employees never get access to it at all.

body.title: Planning Around the Deferral
body.scenario: Vivek is a senior engineer at a DPIIT-recognised, Inter-Ministerial Board certified startup in Bengaluru. He holds 10,000 vested options at a ₹15 exercise price, with the current FMV at ₹265. He is fairly happy in the job but gets calls from recruiters every quarter. The company has never run a buyback and talks vaguely about listing in four to five years.
body.prompt: Should he exercise now under the deferral, and what should he weigh?
body.modelAnswer: The arithmetic first: exercising costs 10,000 × ₹15 = ₹1,50,000, and the perquisite would be 10,000 × ₹250 = ₹25,00,000, carrying roughly ₹7,80,000 of tax at 31.2% that the deferral would postpone. The attraction is obvious, but the deferral is tied to staying, and he is being courted every quarter. If he exercises now and moves in two years, the tax falls due on resignation with no sale to fund it, so he would have paid ₹1,50,000 up front and owe ₹7,80,000 on shares with no buyer. The deferral is most valuable to someone confident of staying through a liquidity event, and least valuable to someone likely to move. A middle path is to exercise a portion he could fund the tax on unaided, keeping the rest as unexercised options, and revisit when a buyback or listing becomes concrete rather than vague. He should also confirm in writing that the certification is current, since eligibility is assessed against the company’s status, not its reputation.

children.text: A Note on Rates and Dates

Two details reported for the Income-tax Act, 2025 regime are worth flagging for your own confirmation. First, the window for shares allotted on or after 1 April 2026 is described as 60 months from the end of the
tax year

of allotment, up from 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year under the old provision. Second, the rate applied when the deferred tax finally falls due is described as the rate in force for the tax year of allotment, rather than the rate of the year the trigger occurs. Both come from professional commentary rather than the bare section text, so check the current position before relying on either.

markDefs.definition: The term the Income-tax Act, 2025 uses for the annual period over which income is measured, replacing the previous year and assessment year framework.

points: The deferral postpones ESOP perquisite tax. It never reduces it.
It requires an eligible startup under Section 140 [Section 80-IAC], meaning DPIIT recognition plus an Inter-Ministerial Board certificate.
Reported figures suggest only around 2% of recognised startups hold that certificate, so most employees cannot use this at all.
Payment falls due on the earliest of window expiry, sale of the shares, or ceasing to be an employee.
Resignation is the trigger that catches most people, since it arrives with no cash to pay the tax.
For an allotment with a ₹10,00,000 perquisite, roughly ₹3,12,000 of tax is postponed, while the exercise price is still payable today.
Ask for written confirmation of eligibility before planning any exercise around this relief.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice. The deferral rules, window length and rate treatment described here are drawn from professional commentary on the Income-tax Act, 2025 and were in flux around its commencement. Eligibility is company specific and assessed by the authorities, not by your employer’s description of itself. Confirm the current position with a qualified professional before acting.
